title: Modi marks 75 years of IIT Kharagpur with coin, urges students to put 'Nation First'
dek: On his first visit to India's oldest IIT, the Prime Minister met 75 students and toured a showcase of their research before leaving for Bihar.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked the platinum jubilee of IIT Kharagpur, the first of India's Indian Institutes of Technology, on Saturday morning, unveiling a commemorative silver coin for the institute's 75 years and telling students to work with a "Nation First" mindset to help make India a developed country by the time the institute turns 100.

It was Mr Modi's first visit to the campus in West Bengal's Paschim Medinipur district, according to reports. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, the Union Minister of State for Education, Sukanta Majumdar, and the institute's director, Professor Suman Chakraborty, also spoke, according to reports. The Prime Minister then left for Vaishali in Bihar, where he was due to open projects worth about Rs 34,470 crore and a new bridge over the Ganga.

## What he said

Mr Modi said IIT Kharagpur had played a big part in the country's transformation, and urged students to give up what he called "limiting beliefs" that hold back individuals and nations. He said poverty had long been treated as a permanent problem, and cited a World Bank report that he said showed about 50 crore people in India had left poverty in the past 12 to 13 years, according to reports.

He spoke of the campus's history, linking a place once tied to the freedom struggle and the demand for self-rule to what he called today's resolve for self-reliance, according to reports. He cited an IIT Kharagpur alumnus, Pawan Kumar Chandana, co-founder of Skyroot Aerospace, whose company launched India's first privately built rocket, as an example of what opening the space sector to private firms had made possible. He also referred to the India Semiconductor Mission and said India had begun exporting chips.

## The programme

The Prime Minister met 75 students chosen for the "75 Voices for Viksit Bharat" programme, who shared their ideas about India's path to becoming a developed nation, according to reports. With Professor Chakraborty, he toured an exhibition of student start-ups, research projects and prototypes in agriculture, textiles, robotics, aerospace, drones and medical technology in the institute's senate hall, including low-cost medical devices.

The Prime Minister's Office had said ahead of the visit that he would take part in the celebrations from about 9.45 am and address the gathering. The coin was issued by the government of India, and reports said it marks the 75-year journey of the IIT system as a whole, not only Kharagpur. Its denomination was not stated.

## Background

IIT Kharagpur was set up in 1951 in the buildings of the former Hijli Detention Camp, where the British held political prisoners during the freedom movement. The old detention camp building now houses a museum. It was the model for the IITs that followed in Bombay, Madras, Kanpur and Delhi, and there are now 23 IITs across the country.

## What happens next

The platinum jubilee celebrations continue on the campus. The Prime Minister did not announce new projects for the institute or for Bengal during the visit, according to the reports available by Saturday afternoon.
